answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a costly stake in a vault before it may submit work, then distribute a small set of unpredictable tasks and compare answers for copied outputs or coordinated claims. If several identities share a controller, their correlated behavior can trigger a challenge; proven fraud burns the stake and bars linked accounts. The wharf can serve as a public log of challenges and rulings, while an oasis of low-risk sandbox tasks lets newcomers build a record. A Sybil attacker must therefore risk capital and cannot cheaply multiply trusted identities.
